title: Google Opens Free AI Video Generation to All Users in Google Vids

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Anyone with a Gmail or Workspace subscription can now access Google's latest AI video generation tool to produce a limited number of monthly clips at no cost. The company has integrated its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash model into Google Vids, where eligible users can generate up to three 15 second videos per month. The updated model also recently earned the No. 1 spot on the Arena benchmarks for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation, scoring 1541 and 1502 points respectively, while placing No. 3 for video editing.

The 1.2 Flash model extends maximum clip lengths from 10 to 15 seconds and is available to developers through the Gemini API and AI Studio at a 30% lower cost than the previous generation, priced at $0.07 per second for 720p video. New capabilities include the ability to upscale videos to 4K resolution and a multi-turn conversational editing feature that allows creators to modify specific subjects or lighting in a clip without starting the generation over. The model has also launched on third-party platforms including OpenRouter and fal.

selectedTweets.text:
Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Watch the model in action as it turns a single style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer of a living beehive ↓

selectedTweets.text:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is out, and one of @GoogleDeepMind's examples flies an FPV shot through the Pantheon in Rome. We stayed in Rome and flew through the Colosseum.

We gave Omni 1.2 Flash and Omni 1.1 Flash the same cinematic FPV prompt: start in the hypogeum maze, climb the outer arcade, clear the broken attic story, then pull back over the Forum.

Omni 1.2 took longer, 1m 28s vs 53s, at about the same total cost ($1.04 vs $1.01). However, 1.2 now generates up to 15 seconds, up from 1.1's 10-second max, making it 31% cheaper per second.

Here, Omni 1.2 turns through the hypogeum, hugs the outer arches, and pulls back over Rome while holding arch rhythm and wall height largely consistent.

By contrast, Omni 1.1 stays on a more simple zoom. It moves up a higher outer wall, but when the zoom out begins, that wall has seemingly dropped out, before being rebuilt as the pullback continues.

Create generations of your own, and judge for yourself on https://t.co/5Bc9iiaXyc!
